issues: What standard of review applies to a federal tribunal's interpretation of its own governing statute on judicial review

Whether any exceptions to presumptive reasonableness review apply (legislated standard of review, statutory rights of appeal, rule of law issues such as constitutional questions or jurisdictional boundaries between tribunals)
What the reasonableness standard requires in reviewing a tribunal's statutory interpretation
Whether the tribunal's decision bears the hallmarks of reasonableness (justification, transparency, intelligibility) in light of the statutory text, context, and purpose
key_facts: A federal administrative tribunal interpreted its own home statute
The client disputes the correctness of that interpretation
Client is seeking judicial review of the tribunal's decision
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review of a federal tribunal decision
candidate_statutes: Administrative Tribunals Support Service of Canada Act
search_terms: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov
rule of law jurisdictional lines between tribunals
statutory right of appeal standard of review Vavilov
needs_clarification: What is the tribunal's enabling/governing statute, and does it provide a statutory right of appeal (which could change the standard of review from reasonableness to appellate standards)?
